name: Goretek CorpSec Field Loadout Mk-7
description: Head-to-toe CorpSec field kit: matte-black ballistic-rated helmet with integrated AR visor and neural port passthrough, gorget collar sealing against chem particulate. Torso runs a Goretek TacShell-derived hard-plate vest over a moisture-wicking compression underlayer with spinal-rig channel running center-back. Mid-layer is a dark charcoal ops jacket, mag-closure, with chrome-arm sleeve splits. Reinforced cargo trousers in graphite ripstop, knee-pad inserts, thigh holster mounts. Boots are steel-toe mag-lock tactical with ankle-brace integration for leg prosthetics. All hardware matte-finished to suppress EM signature.
functionality: Full ballistic protection to Class-3 threat rating; spinal-rig channel accommodates most standard military augments; chrome-arm sleeve splits; integrated AR visor with BCI uplink; mag-lock boot sole for vertical surface operations; chem-seal gorget.
what_it_says: This person is contracted, armed, and authorized — approach with stated business only.
story_hooks: A field kit with a serial number that traces back to a decommissioned unit — the wearer shouldn't exist in any active roster.
The AR visor keeps overlaying a ghost contact that was deleted from the network six months ago.
CorpSec insignia has been field-stripped and replaced with blank panels — someone's operating off-book.

physical_description.visual_profile: Imposing full-body tactical silhouette: a human-shaped fortress of matte-black and charcoal layers, angular and utilitarian. The figure reads as armored corporate authority—broad shoulders from the hard-plate vest, tapered waist from compression layers, straight-legged stance stabilized by reinforced boots. The integrated helmet dominates, giving an inhuman, sealed-off presence.
physical_description.fit: Form-fitting compression base with intentionally oversized tactical jacket layered over hard-plate vest for mobility under armor. Cargo trousers sit at natural waist, cut straight to accommodate thigh holster rigs. Boots are snug at ankle with rigid ankle-brace channels. Overall: engineered for function over flattery, every element locked into position.
physical_description.primary_material: Ballistic weave composite (helmet and vest), moisture-wicking synthetic compression (underlayer), ripstop graphite canvas (trousers), matte-anodized aluminum alloys (hardware and chrome arm-sleeve panels)
physical_description.texture: Helmet: smooth composite shell with recessed visor line. Vest: rigid segmented plating with elasticated gussets. Jacket: slightly pebbled synthetic leather with chrome-smooth arm panels. Trousers: fine ripstop weave with reinforced knee patches of denser ballistic fabric. Boots: scuffed industrial-grade synthleather.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black primary (helmet, vest plating), dark charcoal secondary (jacket, trousers), graphite accents (inner layers visible at seams), chrome-silver arm panels and mag-closures for tactical contrast
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap jacket closure (silent operation), friction-fit helmet seal at gorget collar, belt-loop + compression-snap trousers, mag-lock ankle straps on boots, integrated neural-port passthrough (sealed magnetic coupling at helmet rear)
distinctive_features: Integrated AR visor with matte-black anti-glare coating
Neural port passthrough at helmet occiput for direct command-feed
Gorget collar with chem-particulate sealing gasket
Spinal-rig channel running center-back of vest for data/power conduits
Thigh holster mounting brackets (standard Goretek universal slots)
Knee-pad insert pockets (field-replaceable ceramic or ballistic foam)
Mag-lock boot coupling for prosthetic integration (ankle-brace compatible)
Matte-finished all hardware (suppresses EM and thermal signature)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 corporate luxury: only top-tier CorpSec operatives, executive protection, and special-operations contractors can afford Goretek Mk-7. Price point: Φ45,000+ for full loadout.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this signals: I am corporate-authorized lethal force. Corpo security, not street muscle. The integrated tech and EM-suppression indicate counter-hacking capability and corporate espionage/counter-espionage work. Wearer is either highly trained enforcement or a corpo exec paranoid enough to fund their own protection.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine or battle-worn with extreme visibility: scuffed boots, scorched vest plates, cracked visor replacements, frayed mag-closure edges. No middle ground—either just-issued or heavily deployed. Field units show tape-reinforced seams and swapped-out knee-pad inserts.

image_prompt: A hyper-tactical neo-noir CorpSec operative in full Goretek Mk-7 loadout, standing at 3/4 angle in moody industrial warehouse lighting. Matte-black ballistic helmet with integrated AR visor glowing faint cyan at the visor-line. Dark charcoal ops jacket with visible chrome arm-panel splits catching hard rim-light. Graphite ripstop cargo trousers, reinforced knee pads, steel-toe mag-lock boots. Spinal-rig channel visible down center-back. Model statue-still, weapon-ready stance, harsh shadows defining every angle of the loadout. Background: rain-slicked GLMZ industrial façade, neon corpo logos just out of focus. Cinematic, professional, intimidating. --ar 2:3 --v 6
